sections.h2: How do I sell a house in Waco, TX without waiting months?
sections.html:
The quickest Waco sales are usually direct purchases where the buyer pays cash, accepts the house as it is and closes when the title work is done. A retail listing can reach more buyers, but showings, inspections and lender approval stretch the calendar.

Nearly half of Waco's housing is renter-occupied, so many houses here are held as rentals. If yours has a tenant, mention the lease terms early, since they affect when a buyer can take possession.

  • Fast route: a cash buyer, a short inspection period and a closing date you pick.
  • Open-market route: staging, showings and a buyer whose loan must be approved.
  • Slow route: unresolved liens, an open estate or a tenant who will not leave.

sections.h2: Where is Waco and what shaped it?
sections.html:
Waco lies in central McLennan County, about seventy miles south of Dallas, close to the point where the Brazos and Bosque rivers join. The Handbook of Texas names Interstate 35, U.S. highways 84 and 77 and State Highway 6 as the main roads.

The first block of the new town was laid out on March 1, 1849, on the old Waco village ground. Cotton carried the early economy, a suspension bridge over the Brazos opened in 1870, and rail lines arrived in 1871 and the early 1880s. Baylor University moved to Waco in 1887, and Paul Quinn College opened in 1872.

The city's history also includes the tornado of May 11, 1953, which killed 114 people and destroyed 196 business buildings. Connally Air Force Base closed in 1966, and an urban renewal program begun in 1958 had channeled more than $125 million into the urban core by 1978. The result is a mix of older central blocks and newer outer neighborhoods.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Waco homes?
sections.html:
Waco's typical owned home is valued at $221,700 in the 2020-2024 estimates, and just 49.4 percent of units are owner-occupied. That split explains why investors are a visible part of the market.

sections.h2: How large is Waco and what drives its economy?
sections.html:
Waco covers 88.73 square miles of land at about 1,561 residents per square mile, a spread-out layout with a short average trip to work of 18.7 minutes. A short commute is worth naming in a listing.

Census data put 2022 retail sales near $3.44 billion, health care and social assistance receipts around $2.04 billion, and accommodation and food services at about $676 million. Hospitals, schools and shopping give the city a base of year-round employers.

With rents around $1,165 a month, a rental-minded buyer will run numbers against that figure. Have the lease, deposit records and recent repair invoices ready.

sections.h2: What happens when Waco property taxes are not paid?
sections.html:
Unpaid property tax is secured by a lien that attaches each January 1, so the debt follows the house, and the city notes that paying back taxes does not make someone the owner. The final remedy is a tax sale.

  • The City of Waco says tax sales happen on the first Tuesday of the month at 2:00 p.m. on the McLennan County Courthouse steps, run by a deputy constable.
  • A property that draws no bid can be struck off to the city, which resells it after a six-month or two-year redemption period.
  • A former owner of non-homestead property can buy back within six months by paying 25 percent of the auction price plus taxes, costs and fees.
  • For homestead or special-use land the buy-back window is two years, at 25 percent in year one and 50 percent in year two.

Ask the McLennan County Tax Office for the amount due before you contract to sell.

sections.h2: What does a Waco seller need to record and prove?
sections.html:
The deed is recorded with the McLennan County Clerk, and it must be acknowledged before a notary or sworn before two witnesses. The state clerk manual lists $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each page after, plus other clerk fees, so confirm the total with the clerk.

School districts must give a $140,000 homestead exemption, with $60,000 extra for owners 65 or older or disabled. A disabled veteran may receive up to $12,000 depending on rating, and a veteran rated 100 percent disabled can receive a total exemption.

For an inherited house, an affidavit of heirship has no court review behind it, and no law forces a title company to accept it. If a tenant will not leave, a justice court case follows written notice, and a writ of possession cannot issue before six days after judgment.

faqs.q: When are Waco tax sales held?
faqs.a: The City of Waco says they take place the first Tuesday of the month at 2:00 p.m. on the courthouse steps and are run by a deputy constable.

faqs.q: Can a former owner reclaim a Waco house after a tax sale?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Non-homestead property can be bought back within six months at 25 percent of the auction price plus costs. Homestead or special-use land has a two-year window with a 25 or 50 percent premium.

faqs.q: Does a tenant slow a Waco sale?
faqs.a: It can. A buyer needs to know the lease term and whether the tenant will stay. If the tenant must leave, the eviction process runs through justice court after written notice.

faqs.q: Who should I ask about the property tax balance on my Waco house?
faqs.a: Ask the McLennan County Tax Office for the amount due and any plan. The appraisal district sets value but does not collect.

faqs.q: How does ownership of an inherited Waco house get documented?
faqs.a: Through probate, a muniment of title, or a transfer on death deed recorded before death. An affidavit of heirship may not satisfy a buyer.
